text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU_POOL_UTIL_HIGH (apac-primary) triggered — queue growth detected, autoscaler not increasing pool. Link: https://redwood/alerts/1999991234

alice: seeing huge tail latency and queued requests in apac-primary. dashboard shows backlog ~11.8k, error rate still low but timeouts creeping. paging oncall.

bob: on it. quick check: autoscaler logs show repeated ScaleUpBlocked: quota_limit_reached. Looks like cloud quota cap hit for apac region GPUs.

alice: can we confirm whether spillover routing to apac-secondary is enabled? I think we saw an overlap earlier where routing policy should steer but might be blocked by variant mismatch.

bob: routing policy is configured to spillover -> apac-secondary, eu-primary as fallback, but the latest deploy added a model-tag filter. apac-secondary doesn't have the model:heavy-llama variant. requests are considered incompatible, so router drops into queued state instead of failover.

carol: paging myself. extracting autoscaler and router logs now.

bob: logs snippet: ```
Autoscaler: ScaleUpBlocked(reason=quota_limit_reached, region=apac-primary, requested=8, available_quota=0)
Routing: candidate_regions=[apac-secondary], compatible=false, mismatch_tags=[model:heavy-llama]
Queue: pending=11842, inflight=320, avg_latency=2.3s
```

dave: customer impact note: a few enterprise customers are seeing slow responses; our monitoring shows SLOs degrading for chat endpoints but no 5xx spikes yet. likely partial degradation.

alice: runbook step 1: confirm quota. step 2: trigger manual spillover toggle (force-ignore-model-tags) while we work with infra to increase quota. step 3: notify affected customers.

carol: confirmed cloud quota is 0 spare GPUs for apac-primary. Request to cloud account team created (ticket #APAC-QUOTA-778). ETA unknown.

bob: executing manual spillover toggle on routing service to allow variant-compatible fallback (temporary, 15m window). Command: ```
curl -X POST "https://router-api/internal/force_spillover" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN" -d '{"from":"apac-primary","to":"apac-secondary","ignore_model_tags":true,"ttl_seconds":900}'
```

ops-bot: runbook action started by bob: force_spillover invoked, request_id=fs-1999-01.

carol: toggled. monitoring: pending queue dropping from 11.8k -> 3.2k in 4m. tail latency improving.

alice: good. start customer comms: template snippet: "We're experiencing capacity constraints in APAC; we've enabled temporary cross-region routing to mitigate. Expect improved latency in ~5-10m. We're working on a permanent capacity bump and will update."

dave: note: need to watch cost and token routing consistency. some requests will incur cross-region egress for customers pinned to apac-primary. ops: flag billing impact for finance.

bob: while spillover is helping, autoscaler still blocked. created an escalation to cloud quota team. If quota ETA > 2h, we'll spin up temporary Dedicated pool in eu-primary and update routing policy to include eu-primary as secondary for heavy-llama.

carol: adding runbook checkpoint: if queue > 10k after 20m of spillover, escalate to SRE lead and enact fallback to eu-primary.

sre-rotation: taking over pager. I'm now the incident owner. summary: apac-primary saturated -> autoscaler blocked by cloud GPU quota. Router prevented spillover due to model tag mismatch; manual spillover enabled and reduced queue. next steps: follow quota escalation, prepare eu-primary fallback plan, communicate with customers.

alice: handoff ack. leaving notes: metrics to watch: pending_queue, avg_latency_95, spillover_rate, egress_bytes_apac->eu. logging: capture one sample request id that experienced fallback for trace.

bob: adding sample id: req_0xa3f4b9. Trace shows request routed to apac-secondary after force_spillover.

carol: issuing mitigation runbook entries: ```
1) Keep force_spillover for now (owner=sre-rotation).
2) If queue <= 2k for 10m, start graceful rollback of ignore_model_tags.
3) If quota not resolved in 60m, update routing to include eu-primary as spillover target: curl -X POST https://router-api/internal/update_policy -d '{"policy":"add_spillover","from":"apac-primary","to":"eu-primary","match_tags":["model:heavy-llama"]}'
4) Document customer-impact in incident doc and send outbound comms.
```

ops-bot: note: cost_estimate for current spillover ~ +$1.2k/h if sustained. Finance notified.

sre-rotation: I'm going to be on this for the next shift. assigning carol as secondary. carol, please keep the manual spillover toggled and monitor for any model-output regressions (quality alerts).

carol: ack. I'll also request a temporary node pool in apac using spot instances while quota sorts out — low priority but may help if allowed.

dave: customer comm sent to affected customers at 1999991420: "Experiencing increased latency; mitigation in progress via cross-region routing. We'll follow up with timeline."

alice: small note: we saw one error from router: 503 when candidate region unreachable; need to add backoff and retry in router to avoid immediate queueing. filing ticket ROUTER-392.

bob: logs show no 5xx from model servers, so feasibility is good. next measurable milestone: pending queue < 1k and avg_latency_95 < 800ms.

sre-rotation: milestone hit at 1999991620: pending queue 780, avg_latency_95 740ms. reducing manual spillover window to 5m to test rollback.

carol: starting rollback test now. rolling ignore_model_tags down in 5..4..3..2..1.

ops-bot: force_spillover TTL reduced to 300s by carol. request_id=fs-1999-01-update.

alice: monitoring: queue held stable ~820 then slowly increased to 1.1k after rollback started. looks like some incompatible requests are still queued.

sre-rotation: decision: re-enable force_spillover for another 30m while we get quota bump. we cannot afford customer-visible regressions.

dave: updating incident status: Mitigated (manual spillover active). Impact: increased latency for APAC customers for ~15-45 minutes; no large-scale errors. Next: quota resolution with cloud and evaluate policy change to avoid tag-mismatch blocking spillover.

sre-rotation: handing off to next oncall at 1999991800 — @dave you are now incident owner for stabilization. If anything degrades, page oncall.

dave: ack takeover. I'll keep the temporary spillover active until cloud quota is confirmed. leaving detailed notes in incident tracker.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: incident owner=dave, severity=SEV2, incident_start=1999991234, mitigation=manual_spillover, current_status=stabilized.

carol: closing Slack thread for now; will post updates as they happen. thanks team. :party_parrot:
